(11) Require a claim for a drug to include a modifier to indicate that the drug is subject to an agreement under 42 U.S.C. § 256b.
(12) Penalize or retaliate against a pharmacist or pharmacy for exercising rights under this chapter or Article 8, Chapter 23, Title 34. For purposes of this subdivision, the conduct prohibited includes any written or verbal communication that a reasonable individual would construe as a threat of penalty or retaliation received before or in the course of exercising rights under this chapter or Article 8, Chapter 23, Title 34.
(13) Prohibit a pharmacist or pharmacy from declining to dispense a drug to a covered individual, or directing a covered individual to another pharmacy, if the reimbursement amount would be lower than the dispensing cost of the pharmacist or pharmacy.
(14) Take retaliatory action against, or impose any penalty on, a pharmacist or pharmacy who declines to dispense a drug to a covered individual under subdivision (13), including cancellation or nonrenewal of a contract, or suit for breach of contract.
(Act 2021-341, §2; Act 2025-136, §2.)

sections.label: Section 27-45A-11 - Pharmacy Benefits Managers - Material Misrepresentations.
sections.text:
Section 27-45A-11
Pharmacy Benefits Managers - Material Misrepresentations.
A pharmacy benefits manager may not knowingly make a material misrepresentation to a covered individual, pharmacist, or pharmacy.
(Act 2021-341, §2.)

sections.label: Section 27-45A-12 - Use of Pharmacy Benefits of a Covered Individual.
sections.text:
Section 27-45A-12
Use of Pharmacy Benefits of a Covered Individual.
A pharmacist or pharmacy that participates in a health benefit plan’s pharmacy network shall process a prescription drug using the pharmacy benefits of the covered individual if failure to do so will result in a higher out-of-pocket cost to the covered individual.
(Act 2021-341, §2.)

sections.label: Section 27-45A-13 - Pharmacy Benefits Managers -- Prohibited Activities Related to Independent Pharmacies; Exceptions.
sections.text:
Section 27-45A-13
Pharmacy Benefits Managers -- Prohibited Activities Related to Independent Pharmacies; Exceptions.
(a) Notwithstanding any other provision of this chapter or any form of a contract to the contrary, with respect to an independent pharmacy, a pharmacy benefits manager, directly or through an affiliate or a contracted third party, may not do any of the following:
(1) Reimburse for dispensing a prescription drug in an amount that is less than the Medicaid reimbursement rate.
(2) Impose a fee or otherwise adjust or lower the reimbursement of a drug at the time the claim is adjudicated, or after the claim is adjudicated, that in any way reduces the amount of reimbursement for the drug as regulated pursuant to subdivision (1).
(3) Increase a covered individual’s cost-sharing percentage or ratio at or after the point of sale by raising the deductible, copayment, or coinsurance, or by requiring any other out-of-pocket payment as a means to recoup the dispensing cost portion of the reimbursement required pursuant to subdivision (1).
(4) Reject payment of a claim for a drug that is submitted by an independent pharmacy when the drug is available to a covered individual at a different in-network pharmacy; provided, however, if the drug is dispensed by the different in-network pharmacy, the pharmacy benefits manager shall pay the independent pharmacy a surcharge equal to the reimbursement that would have been paid pursuant to subdivision (1) had the independent pharmacy dispensed the drug.
(b) A health benefit plan that covers individuals who are public employees and that reimburses independent pharmacies for dispensing prescription drugs during its plan year in an aggregate amount that is higher than would otherwise be calculated using the rate set in subdivision (a)(1), upon proof of the same submitted to the commissioner, shall be exempt from this section.
(Act 2025-136, §3.)

sections.label: Section 27-45A-14 - Pharmacy Benefits Managers -- Regulation of Rebates from Drug Manufacturers.
sections.text:
Section 27-45A-14
Pharmacy Benefits Managers -- Regulation of Rebates from Drug Manufacturers.
A pharmacy benefits manager, either directly or through a PBM affiliate, when performing pharmacy benefits management services or other prescription drug or device services for a health benefit plan client, shall pass on 100 percent of all rebates received, directly or indirectly, from a pharmaceutical manufacturer unless the health benefit plan client directs the pharmacy benefits manager or PBM affiliate to apply the rebates to purchases of prescription drugs by covered individuals at the point of sale or the health benefit plan client directs the pharmacy benefits manager, PBM affiliate, or health insurer to retain a portion of the rebates as an administrative fee.
(Act 2025-136, §4.)
